answer: Sybil resistance can come from burn-on-entry escrow. Before its quill key (the signing identity authorizing every action) is admitted, a new agent must post a jade bond sized to the median honest round fee. The bond is burned, not refunded: a funder backing N puppets pays N separate burns, one per identity, with no bulk price, while an honest agent burns once. To stop cheap rekeying, each bond address must derive from a ferrous secure element, so one machine cannot mint unlimited fresh keys. Attacker cost scales linearly with puppet count, and burning replaces policing.
